pull request.plain: a proposed change to the product, set aside for checking before it joins the real thing
pull request.example: Like a draft of a page you hand to an editor: nothing is printed until the editor agrees.

CI.plain: the automatic checks that run on every change
CI.example: Like the safety inspection a car goes through before it leaves the factory.

merge.plain: to join a checked change into the real product
merge.example: Like adding the edited page into the finished book.

branch.plain: a separate copy of the work where a change is made without touching the real product
branch.example: Like photocopying a recipe so you can try a new spice without spoiling the original.

commit.plain: one saved step of the work, with a short note on what changed
commit.example: Like a numbered save point in a game: you can always go back to it.

review.plain: a second agent reading a change closely to find mistakes before it goes in
review.example: Like a proofreader going through an article before it is published.

slice.plain: one small, finished piece of a bigger feature, built and checked on its own
slice.example: Like building a house room by room rather than all at once.

lane.plain: how much care a piece of work gets: quick, small, feature or bug, each with its own amount of checking
lane.example: Like the express and the full-service checkouts at a shop.

feature flag.plain: a switch that keeps new work hidden from users until you turn it on
feature flag.example: Like a curtain over a new shop window until opening day.

preview.plain: a private copy of the product with the change in it, so you can look before it goes live
preview.example: Like a rehearsal performance before opening night.

worktree.plain: a separate working folder where one agent builds one piece of work without getting in the way of the others
worktree.example: Like giving each builder their own workbench.

STOP.plain: the big red button: every agent stops working until you lift it
STOP.example: Like pulling the emergency cord on a train.

Standard.plain: the normal amount of checking and sign-off for your project's work
Standard.example: Like the usual security at an office, short of what a bank vault needs.

Locked.plain: the strictest setting: the change cannot go ahead without your own sign-off
Locked.example: Like a safe that opens only with your own key.

the helper.plain: the small program on your computer that holds your sign-in and does the things agents are not allowed to do themselves
the helper.example: Like a bank teller who handles the money so the clerks never touch the vault.

the foreman.plain: the agent that runs the building: it hands out pieces of work and keeps them moving
the foreman.example: Like the site manager on a building job, who is not laying bricks but knows who is.

the gate.plain: the final set of checks a change must pass before it can join the product
the gate.example: Like passport control: nobody walks through without being checked.

appetite.plain: how much time and effort you are willing to spend on something
appetite.example: Like deciding a weekend job is worth a weekend, and no more.

the done contract.plain: the list, agreed before building starts, of what must be true for the work to count as finished
the done contract.example: Like the checklist a builder and owner sign before the handover walk-through.
